scope: Audit of corrected Tier1 episode5 Dex-inspired PPO continuation from60M to350M, followed by fresh native FlashSAC5M replay comparison

findings.finding: Evaluation regression is present in saved poses
findings.evidence: All six evaluations were recomputed on CPU from preserved raw poses and mesh samples and matched all four recorded metrics. AUC is nonmonotonic: .1640 at100M, .1989 at300M, .1158 at350M.

findings.finding: Updates improve the assisted training objective
findings.evidence: First/last40 continuation iterations: mean step reward .075604 to .132229, dense reward .138403 to .163686, completed-episode mean length83.51 to182.65. No skipped PPO updates in the continuation. Weighted component sum differs from total by at most2.4734e-8.

Every logged continuation iteration used assistance1.0 and checkpoint curriculum decision history is empty. Final weighted completion .04978 and progress .25079 fail custom thresholds .8/.9. Roughly90.6% of last40 iteration episode endings were classified as palm-tracking failures.

Our gate divides per-step weighted means by dt and weight. DexMachina paper Algorithm1 uses completed-episode cumulative rewards divided by maximum episode length. Its released code also checks episode length, gradients and reward thresholds, and exposes separate gain decay and a zero_epoch fallback. Our80%/90% gates, discrete CHORD scales, early frame-zero reset mixture, whole-body action space and absent forced-zero stage are adaptations, not a faithful reproduction.
findings.implication: High local rewards during short assisted fragments are insufficient evidence of full-sequence capability. This method needs a validated assistance handoff and episode-normalized evidence before further PPO scaling.

findings.finding: Reward and leaderboard emphasize different errors
findings.evidence: Pinned native ReconBody reward includes object_position and palm_orientation but no direct object_orientation term. AUC includes mesh-point displacement from both translation and rotation. Evaluation object rotation error rises64.12deg to73.10deg from300M to350M; position error rises27.98cm to31.02cm.
findings.implication: This is a potential objective mismatch, not proof it alone causes regression; retained unchanged in requested native FlashSAC test.

findings.finding: Learning rate was not manually changed
findings.evidence: Native KL-adaptive PPO produced a continuation LR range about1e-5 to7.59e-5; terminal LR is its configured1e-5 floor. Final40 KL mean .02769 versus desired .02; clipping fraction .3252. These observations do not isolate LR as the cause.

findings.finding: Input identity and native timing checked
findings.evidence: PPO motion SHA matches the earlier corrected native FlashSAC baseline. Both use native50Hz source-frame playback. No WM was involved.

decision: Do not continue or silently alter the failed PPO adaptation. Run requested native FlashSAC350M from scratch on the same input/seed with5M replay and batch2048. An automated typed-config check rejects any learner change beyond replay capacity. Native curriculum reaches zero assistance at209999872 transitions.
limitations: One episode and training seed,16 evaluation worlds. Association and source audit do not establish causal ablations. Local tier-input-reference scores, not official leaderboard values.
